To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) a generalized varying coefficient model is proposed, which is a generalization of varying coefficient models to the case where not only current values, but also past values of the predictors, affect current response; (b) the proposed model is applicable for the case where there is additive measurement error in both response and predictor processes; (c) the proposed model can be used in the case of additive error in the common varying coefficient model;

we propose a new model and a new method of estimation, that the proposed model is more appropriate than the existing ones in some situations and that the new estimation method is more accurate than the existing ones.

the generalized varying coefficient model provides a useful tool for modeling longitudinal data, and that the proposed methodology provides a useful tool to estimate the generalized varying coefficient models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of estimating regression coefficient functions in the context of longitudinal data.
the problem of estimating the effects of a set of predictors, such as time and covariates, on a set of responses.
the development of a generalization of varying coefficient models to cases where the regression coefficient functions have sliding window supports, and estimation in the context thereof.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a generalization for varying coefficient models for time series data and develop an efficient estimation and inference procedure for this model.
we have proposed a generalization of a varying coefficient model to cases where not just the current value of a predictor process, but also the recent values of the predictor affect current response.
we proposed a new model for longitudinal data, called generalized varying coefficient model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed methodology can be applied to a variety of longitudinal models that relate not only current observations of predictors to response, but also to recent past observations.
the proposed model and the associated methodology for estimation and prediction can be used to model and predict longitudinal data when the predictors are subject to measurement errors.
it provides a framework for the estimation of regression functions that have a sliding window support around current time.
